subject.title: Discord DMs: inbound messages silently dropped (outbound works)

question: Should Discord root `allowFrom` be an additive global allowlist for every account, or should account-scoped `allowFrom` remain a restrictive override that only inherits root when unset?
rationale: The direct code repair would change who can DM account-scoped Discord bots, so automation should not choose the authorization boundary without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Preserve restrictive overrides
options.body: Keep account `allowFrom` as the limiting scope when set, and address the user pain through diagnostics, docs, status output, and live-proofed routing guidance.

options.title: Make root allowFrom additive
options.body: Merge root and account `allowFrom` for Discord accounts, accepting that globally allowlisted users may reach accounts that were previously narrower.

options.title: Add explicit inheritance mode
options.body: Introduce a documented policy knob for additive versus restrictive account allowlists, with migration and upgrade tests for both modes.

recommendation.title: Preserve restrictive overrides
recommendation.body: Keep account `allowFrom` as the limiting scope when set, and address the user pain through diagnostics, docs, status output, and live-proofed routing guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Discord DM access and shared allowlist resolver history points to this person as the best available owner for the security-sensitive contract choice.
